clues: This city sits on the Oldman River, to the south east of Calgary. It is not far from the line with the United States.
The high peaks close to this city shape its weather. Summers here are warm, winters are mild, and the wind blows a lot.
Its growth began with drift mines that dug coal in the late eighteen hundreds. Farm work then helped it grow more in the next years.
This place is home to a school that stands all on its own in the south. It is the only university in all of Alberta south of Calgary.
This city is the heart of southern Alberta for trade, schools, banks, jobs and travel. It is the main hub that serves the whole south of the province.
